actors: SFC, which authorises funds and makes case-specific complex-product designations.
Fund manager, which reviews classification and communicates with distributors.
Distributors, which apply the applicable sale requirements.
Investors receiving distributions of the Fund.
Home regulators, whose conditions may inform SFC discretion.
classification_assumptions: The assessment concerns one fund at one identified distribution assessment time; listed closed-ended alternative asset funds are excluded.
Direct exposure, indirect exposure and positive NAV are supplied as exact integers in the same valuation unit at that time, under a separately established aggregation methodology.
Indirect exposure covers all relevant instruments and underlying private credit or private equity; the listed examples are not an exhaustive instrument whitelist.
A designation input records an actual SFC decision applicable at the assessment time; scrutiny, risk characteristics and home-regulator restrictions do not themselves establish designation.
The result answers whether a classification basis under this circular is present. It does not determine historical classification persistence, overall distribution compliance or legal approval.

citations.quote: This circular provides guidance to management companies of funds that are authorised by the SFC for offering to the public in Hong Kong (Funds)6 in this regard.

A Fund will be considered as a complex product if its total direct and indirect exposures to private market assets amount to 50% or more of the Fund’s NAV. On a case-by-case basis, the SFC may also designate a Fund as a complex product, taking into account factors including, without limitation:
In assessing whether the complex product designation is warranted7, the SFC will adopt a holistic approach taking into account the specific circumstances of the case.
In cases where the Fund’s aggregate direct and indirect exposures to private market assets are less than 50% of the Fund’s NAV.
Except for listed closed-ended alternative asset funds (LAFs).
The examples of indirect exposures set out in paragraph 1 above are non-exhaustive, and subject to review and update by the SFC from time to time in view of market developments.

A Fund classified as a complex product will be subject to the SFC’s prevailing requirements for the sale of complex products8 including but not limited to ensuring the suitability of the Fund for its investors irrespective of whether solicitation or recommendation is involved.

reading.distinction: Inspection of both prior models found that they already distinguish the relevant actors, underlying assets, intermediate instruments, fund-wide aggregation, exclusions and operative designation. No source-supported rival threshold rule was identified. The consequential remaining distinction is between a contemporaneous classification basis and an enduring classification status: a below-threshold snapshot without an operative designation does not resolve the effect of an earlier threshold crossing. Missing evidence also differs from evidence that a classification basis is absent. The proposal therefore retains the two classification routes while expressly limiting the question answered.

reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Does an in-scope Fund have a contemporaneous complex-product classification basis under this circular? True means aggregate direct and indirect private-market exposure is at least 50% of NAV or an operative SFC designation exists, requiring complex-product treatment on that basis. False means both bases are absent on established facts; it does not establish declassification following an earlier threshold crossing or non-complex status under other rules. Unknown inputs remain unknown unless an independently established branch determines the result. Out-of-scope funds receive no answer. This predicate confers no legal approval.
reading.subject: Contemporaneous fund-level classification basis for distribution

relationships: The fund holds direct investments and intermediate instruments that expose it to underlying private market assets.
All relevant direct and indirect exposure is aggregated against the same fund's NAV; individual holdings and investor transactions are not separate threshold units.
The mandatory threshold includes equality at 50%.
The SFC may designate a below-threshold fund after holistic consideration; discretionary factors are not automatic designation predicates.
Complex-product classification brings applicable sale requirements into play irrespective of solicitation or recommendation.
Managers communicate classification information to distributors; communication is distinct from the classification basis itself.
proposals.temporal_basis: One identified assessment time using contemporaneous exposure and NAV and a designation applicable then. Historical persistence and automatic declassification are not determined by the supplied text.
proposals.unit_of_assessment: One entire fund as a distributed product at the assessment time.

unresolved: Both supplied prior models were inspected. No consequential rival based on omitted actors, components or aggregation quantifiers is supported by the retained text; a second proposal would manufacture ambiguity.
The retained source supplies no rule determining whether classification persists after exposure falls below 50%. A historical-status model cannot be completed without that rule.
The SFC's prospective holistic judgment cannot be computed from the non-exhaustive factors using this expression fragment; an actual designation must be established separately.
Exposure measurement and the content of missing dependencies remain unresolved. Neither the prior models nor this proposal establishes legal completeness.
